label: copy-phase input c (fed-back c), middle of the recall
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, almost only when the fed-back input token is c (98% of activation mass has in_tok c; small amounts on t and e). Never fires in the original phase or at <DEL>, so it is not responding to c the first time it appears. Magnitude depends on position: activations peak at recall_idx 3-4 (steps t=10-13, the c being original token 2 or 3) and in long sequences (L 8-9). They are weak or absent at recall_idx <= 2 and near the end of the copy (to_go 0-1). The top examples are all c as original token 2, re-entered at step L+3. Precision is limited: many fed-back c inputs at the same positions stay silent, and no per-step variable I tested separated those cases. The simplest predicate (copy phase and in_tok c) has recall 0.96 and mass recall 0.98 but precision 0.17. Adding the position window brings precision to 0.48 with mass recall 0.84.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token (most: c, t, e, z, w, j; least: b, l, h, u) and the token being output, by phase (copy phase: t, c, e, j; input phase: ; delimiter step: ); timing cues that raise it most: recall_idx=3, recall_idx=4, t=12.
